data.turoyo: w mədli l u šalfo w aṯino, me bəṯre dewo da knəflile ḥa, frəṭli gawe w qṭili.
data.translation: faßte das Messer und kam heran. Einem der Wölfe verpasste ich eins mit dem Messer, schlitzte ihm den Bauch auf und tötete ihn.

rationale: Thin impact cell; knife context and recipient suffix clarify the meaning, while the precise referent of ḥa remains a question.

data.turoyo: Omər, lu ḥafrit, mədle u kurrəko, knəfle bi pečakke, aṯi, maḥatle bu darbo du aḥuno, hiye aṯoyo mu ṣaydo.
data.translation: Danahm der Unhold den Jungen, wickelte ihn in windeln und legte ihn auf den Weg des Bruders, als er von der Jagd kam.

rationale: Thin wrapping cell; boy as understood patient and explicit cloth b-phrase, with a recoverable whole sentence.

data.turoyo: knəflele lakmo l feme d Nari, twəlle tre ʕarše me diḏe
data.translation: gab Nari einen Schlag aufs Maul, daß ihm zwei Zähne zerbrachen,

rationale: Thin impact cell; overt blow noun plus mouth goal and recipient. The team already treats impact as a numbered sense, so no duplicate light-verb idiom is required.

before: platzen lassen auf (what is it?), verpassen;
after: einen Schlag versetzen, verpassen; etwas gegen ein Ziel schleudern (mit b- oder l-);
rationale: The inherited platzen lassen auf is explicitly questioned. A stone directed at a head, a knife strike and overt lakmo delivered to a mouth establish impact/delivering a blow, not causing something to burst.

summary: Sense 2 is clarified from the Turoyo impact frames: implicit stone with b-head target, a knife context with recipient -le, and explicit lakmo with l-mouth target. The stone’s later fall into a butter jar does not make bursting the lexical meaning of knf.
knəflile segments compatibly as knəf-li-le (agent and recipient). Do not assign it to the separate knfl root merely because its surface contains fl.
The impact/blow construction is already a numbered sense in this entry. The overt lakmo item therefore supplies a sense-2 example rather than a new collocation with a duplicate meaning.

The proposed Detransitive knifi-la at 65/211 has no corroborating form in this packet and competes with the edition’s active wrapping interpretation. The exact source is retained in the input and one occurrence decision, but no unsupported form box or Detransitive sense is published.
The existing note about Midən and 2/19 is preserved verbatim. These six occurrences do not establish a dialect distribution.
At 65/211, is knifila Detransitive plural knifi plus dative -la, or an active form with feminine object? Confirm against the edition or a native speaker before establishing a new Detransitive box.
In JL 11.12/6, does overt tre=ǧule denote cloths wrapped around an omitted pot, or cloths folded/arranged? The German parenthesis supplies the around relation.
Does ḥa in knəflile ḥa (91/29) count a blow or identify one wolf? The broader knife-impact reading is secure, but this internal argument analysis is withheld.
Does sense 2 require forceful hurling in the stone context, or more generally landing a blow? The revised gloss allows the attested impact frames without asserting that every token entails throwing.

Wrapping can specify the covered body/person with b-material, or state two cloths while leaving the pot unexpressed. The latter roles are uncertain and do not yet justify a separate fold/arrange sense.
